issues.description: Column alias discrepancy: The problem statement (instruction at problem_statement.md line 102) explicitly tells students not to rename columns using AS unless requested ('benenne keine mit Spalten mit AS, wenn du nicht dazu aufgefordert wirst'). The reference solution (solution_repository/aufgabe04.sql) uses an alias on the regierungsbezirk column ('SELECT regierungsbezirk AS District, SUM(einwohner_w), SUM(einwohner_m)'). This presents an identifier-naming inconsistency: the problem forbids using AS but the solution demonstrates an alias, which can confuse students about the allowed column names and may cause the automated column-name checks to fail or be unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Preferred fix: remove the alias from the solution so it matches the instruction — change the solution line to 'SELECT regierungsbezirk, SUM(einwohner_w), SUM(einwohner_m) ...'. Alternatively, if the alias is intentional, update the problem statement to explicitly allow or require the alias 'District' for this task and update the tests to expect that column name.

issues.description: The concept 'Regierungsbezirk' (administrative district) is referred to differently across artifacts: the problem statement uses the German term 'Regierungsbezirk' (problem_statement.md), while the solution SQL selects the same column but renames it with an English alias 'District' (solution_repository/aufgabe04.sql: SELECT regierungsbezirk AS District ...). The template file for Aufgabe 04 is an empty stub. This inconsistent output column name (regierungsbezirk vs. District) can confuse students who are asked to group and show the 'Regierungsbezirk' and may also cause automated column-name checks to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent with the problem statement. Remove the English alias in the solution (change SELECT regierungsbezirk AS District, ... to SELECT regierungsbezirk, ...) or explicitly alias it to the original German term (e.g. SELECT regierungsbezirk AS regierungsbezirk or AS Regierungsbezirk) so the output column name matches the term used in the problem description.
